title: Launch Liaison Checklist: Orchestrating Risk, Release Notes, and Rollback Coordination
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Provide a single-runbook liaison checklist to coordinate release notes, cross-team go-to-market tasks, and rapid rollback/incident comms for the runtime-1.22 launch. This ticket defines the gating criteria, owner roles, explicit deliverables for Engineering/Docs/Design/Support, and communication templates. Scope: public API changes and runtime-side performance optimizations shipped via the hosted API and Dedicated. Out of scope: private on-prem packaging and billing changes. Goals: 1) Ensure release notes are accurate, customer-facing bullet points with breaking-change callouts. 2) Define a clear decision ladder for rollback with metric thresholds and owners. 3) Pre-assign liaison contacts for on-call, docs, SDKs, and comms so we can execute a rollback in <30 minutes if required. Acceptance criteria: - Release notes have verified examples and migration steps in the docs PR. - Rollback playbook validated in dry-run and time-to-rollback measured. - Stakeholder RACI confirmed and distributed. - Communication templates reviewed by legal/security where applicable. High-level plan: 1) T-minus 7d: Draft release notes and internal technical summary. 2) T-minus 3d: Cross-team review of notes & rollback runbook; confirm canaries and monitoring dashboards. 3) T-minus 1d: Final sign-off, publish release-candidate notes to drafts, freeze non-critical merges. 4) Launch day: Execute rollout with liaison stationed in #launch-coordination; 60-minute high-sensitivity monitoring window with SLAs for mitigations. Rollback decision triggers (examples): - Error rate spike > 3x baseline sustained for 5m AND latency P95 > 2x SLO; - Customer-reported data corruption or security finding; - Memory/oom or GPU saturation causing >20% capacity loss for >10m. Rollback steps (short): 1) Triage & confirm trigger (on-call eng). 2) Notify PM liaison and release lead. 3) Execute rollback (ops engineer) to last-known-good model/runtime snapshot. 4) Run smoke tests; if green, notify customers and resume traffic. Owner roles (liaison): - Release Lead (PM): Marco Nguyen - Rollback Exec (Eng): Priya Menon - Docs owner: Emily Rodriguez - Design/ux notification: Jonas Park - Support escalation: Kavita Shah - Legal/security approver: Daniel Bloom Release notes coordination tasks: - Engineering: Provide exact API diffs, sample request/response, and migration snippets (due T-3d). - Docs: Produce the customer-facing FAQ and migration guide; include code snippets from SDK owners. - SDK: Create compatibility note and patch release with examples. - Support: Prepare canned responses and triage playbook. Cross-team deliverables & owners: - Monitoring dashboards (ENG-81234) — Eng. - Canary rollout plan & percentage schedule — Eng/PM. - Changelog summary (public) — PM/Docs. - Internal incident template (internal SLAs) — PM/Support. Communication templates (to be copied and used): - Incident alert (internal): "[SEV?] Runtime-1.22: {short description} | Trigger: {metric} | ETA for mitigation: {ETA} | Action: {action owner}" - Customer notification (initial): "We are investigating increased latency impacting API requests; customers may see timeouts. We're actively rolling back a recent change and will provide updates within 30 minutes. Status: {link to status page}." - Rollback complete (customer): "Update: We have rolled back the runtime change for your region. Services are returning to normal; please retry requests. For persistent errors open a ticket {support link}." Decision trade-offs considered: - Full immediate rollback vs. partial region rollback: chose partial first where possible to reduce blast radius but prepared full rollback if cross-region metrics deteriorate. - Automated vs manual rollback: kept rollback manual with automated checkpoints to avoid accidental flip-flops during noisy signals. Notes: legal requested the customer wording avoid absolutes; security requested additional logging on any rollback path that touches PII. Both are incorporated in the templates. Next steps: finalize the release-notes PR, complete the dry-run checklist, and schedule a 30-min prelaunch hop-on at T-minus 2 hours.
